newsitem.title: USA: Gay couples in Hawaii get domestic partner rights.
newsitem.headline: Gay couples in Hawaii get domestic partner rights.

text.p: Homosexual couples in Hawaii on Wednesday began exercising their rights to joint health insurance and property ownership under a new law that guarantees them many of the same benefits as married couples.

The measure also applies to other domestic partners who cannot marry, such as a widowed mother and her son or daughter. It took effect Tuesday after Hawaii Gov. Benjamin Cayetano let it become law without his signature.
Cayetano said he wanted the law to enable gay couples to provide for one another, but had reservations about extending those same rights to non-gay domestic partners.
Although the new law gives gay couples more benefits, it was passed in an attempt to block their right to marry.

Lamakers agreed to the compromise fearing the courts were getting closer to upholding the rights of gay couples to marry. A Hawaii Circuit Court judge ruled in December that banning same-sex marriage was unjustified discrimination, but suspended an order legalising the practice until it was appealed. The matter is now before the state's Supreme Court.
State legislators also have agreed to put on the ballot a proposed amendment to the state constitution that would restrict same-sex marriages. Residents will vote on that proposal in November 1998.
On Wednesday, the state's Health Department said it already had issued 45 certificates to couples seeking reciprocal benefts.

The new law gives domestic partners 60 new benefits, including workers compensation, hospital visitation rights, auto insurance coverage, mental health commitment approvals, and family and funeral leave.
